titulo.alumno: Separating context and a completed action

intro: Learn to alternate accurately between tenses in a story: imperfetto for the setting and passato prossimo for the single event.

piezas.titulo: The boundary between state and event
texto: The **imperfetto** holds up the scene: it describes the conditions, the time and what was going on (*Pioveva forte*, *Cucinavo la cena*).
The **passato prossimo** breaks into the scene with a single event: *È suonato il telefono*, *È arrivato Marco*.

Changing tense changes the perspective: **Pioveva quando è arrivato Marco** (it was already raining in the background when Marco arrived); whereas **Ha piovuto per due ore** presents the rain as a complete, bounded event.

filas.texto: Ieri ha piovuto tutto il pomeriggio.
Ho letto il libro in tre giorni.
Ero stanco, così sono andato a letto.

frases.estudio: Luca, che cosa è successo ieri sera a casa tua?
frases.alumno: Luca, what happened last night at your place?

frases.estudio: Mentre cucinavo la cena, è suonato il telefono.
frases.alumno: While I was cooking dinner, the phone rang.
And who was on the phone?

frases.estudio: Era Marco! Fuori pioveva e non aveva l'ombrello.
frases.alumno: It was Marco! It was raining outside and he didn't have an umbrella.

frases.estudio: Che bella sorpresa! E lui è venuto a cena?
frases.alumno: What a nice surprise! And did he come for dinner?

frases.estudio: Sì, è entrato in casa e abbiamo mangiato insieme.
frases.alumno: Yes, he came in and we ate together.

piezas.titulo: Vocabulary: narrative contrast of past tenses

pregunta.texto: In the sentence «Pioveva quando è arrivato Marco», what role does «pioveva» play?

opciones.texto: It describes the weather that was ongoing when he arrived.
opciones.explicacion: The imperfetto paints the background situation on which the single event falls.

opciones.texto: It says it started raining exactly when Marco arrived.
opciones.explicacion: «Pioveva» shows that the rain was already falling before.

opciones.texto: It expresses a future action forecast by the weather report.
opciones.explicacion: The verb is in the past, not the future.

pregunta.texto: Which tense does the interrupting action take in «Mentre cucinavo, ___ il telefono»?

opciones.explicacion: The single event that interrupts the action in progress requires the passato prossimo.
It would express a continuous sound with no sense of a single interrupting event.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the right form to describe the weather.

frase.texto: ___ quando è arrivato Marco a casa mia.

opciones.explicacion: The weather setting that was ongoing during an arrival is expressed in the imperfetto.
It would present the rain as something that had already finished before Marco arrived.

frase.texto: Mentre cucinavo, è suonato il telefono di casa.

opciones.texto: I was cooking when suddenly the phone rang.
opciones.explicacion: «Mentre cucinavo» marks the process in progress and «è suonato» the single event.

opciones.texto: The phone rang before I came into the kitchen.
opciones.explicacion: It rang while I was cooking.

opciones.texto: First I cooked dinner and then I phoned myself.
opciones.explicacion: The one who was cooking was not the one who called.

pregunta.texto: How do the two tenses combine?

frase.texto: Ieri sera pioveva, ma siamo usciti insieme.

opciones.texto: «Pioveva» describes the bad weather and «siamo usciti» narrates the single decision taken.
opciones.explicacion: The standard alternation between descriptive setting (imperfetto) and event (passato prossimo).

opciones.texto: Both actions were long-lasting habits repeated every week.
opciones.explicacion: Going out last night was a single event («ieri sera»).

opciones.texto: We didn't go out because it was raining hard.
opciones.explicacion: The text clearly says they did go out together.

frase.texto: Mentre leggevo il libro è entrata Sara

piezas.traduccion: While I was reading the book, Sara came in.
piezas.explicacion: Process in the imperfetto interrupted by a single event in the passato prossimo.

pregunta.texto: Why do you say «Mentre camminavo ho visto un amico» and not «Mentre ho camminato...»?

opciones.texto: Because «mentre» frames an action in progress during which another event occurs.
opciones.explicacion: The conjunction «mentre» requires the imperfetto to mark the time background.

opciones.texto: Because «camminare» is a verb that lacks a passato prossimo.
opciones.explicacion: All regular verbs form the passato prossimo.

opciones.texto: Because the verb «vedere» can only be used in the present tense.
opciones.explicacion: «Ho visto» is correctly in the passato prossimo.
